fullPassage: Ancient Athens was home to the first democracy, and it produced some great thinkers. As democracy started to fail, the philosophers of the time tried to figure out why and to think of ways to fix it. One of these philosophers was Plato(427-347 B.C.), a student of Socrates(469-399 B.C.). Plato began to doubt the democracy of his time and tried to think of a better option. In one of his most famous works, The Republic, Plato proposed his ideal society. It was based on what he saw as the four virtues of the state: wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice. He designated a different class of people to fulfill three of these virtues. The wise would rule as “philosopher kings,” the brave would act as “guardians,” the self-disciplined would do “manual work,” and the whole of society would work together toward justice. Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite. If the individual is governed more by the rational element, he or she is suited to rule. Someone who is governed by the will would make a good guardian, and a person governed by the appetite would make a good worker. The ultimate goals of society, for Plato, were fulfillment of needs and happiness. Everyone has needs, and everyone has abilities. But people don’t have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs. Therefore, he felt, society must work together to satisfy the needs of all people. When everyone specializes in their occupation and then exchanges the fruits of their labor with others, all people can meet their needs and be happy. Crucially, Plato believed that the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato’s Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people. Although its aim seems too impractical to become reality, his thoughts laid the foundations of Western philosophy.

questions.passage: Ancient Athens was home to the first democracy, and it produced some great thinkers. As democracy started to fail, the philosophers of the time tried to figure out why and to think of ways to fix it. One of these philosophers was Plato(427-347 B.C.), a student of Socrates(469-399 B.C.). Plato began to <u>doubt</u> the democracy of his time and tried to think of a better option. In one of his most famous works, The Republic, Plato proposed his ideal society. It was based on what he saw as the four virtues of the state: wisdom, courage, self-discipline, and justice. He designated a different class of people to fulfill three of these virtues. The wise would rule as “philosopher kings,” the brave would act as “guardians,” the self-disciplined would do “manual work,” and the whole of society would work together toward justice. Plato saw people as being naturally inclined to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite. If the individual is governed more by the rational element, he or she is suited to rule. Someone who is governed by the will would make a good guardian, and a person governed by the appetite would make a good worker. The ultimate goals of society, for Plato, were fulfillment of needs and happiness. Everyone has needs, and everyone has abilities. But people don’t have the range of abilities required to meet all of their individual needs. Therefore, he felt, society must work together to satisfy the needs of all people. When everyone specializes in their occupation and then exchanges the fruits of their labor with others, all people can meet their needs and be happy. Crucially, Plato believed that the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato’s Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people. Although its aim seems too impractical to become reality, his thoughts laid the foundations of Western philosophy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 doubt와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: doubt=의심하다 / trust=신뢰하다 / accept=받아들이다 / question=의문을 제기하다 / prove=증명하다

① trust: 신뢰하다 — doubt의 반대예요

② accept: 받아들이다 — 의심과 반대예요

③ question: 의문을 제기하다 — doubt(의심하다)의 동의어 ←정답

④ prove: 증명하다 — 의미가 달라요
det.tip: began to doubt democracy = question (의문을 품다).

questions.passage:
(A) In Plato's theory, a person governed by the <u>will</u> is spirited and brave, so such a person would make a good guardian.

(B) She made a <u>will</u> before she died, leaving all her property to her children.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 will의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: will: (A) 의지, 기개 (B) 유언장
det.analysis:
① (A) 의지 (B) 유언장: (A)는 플라톤이 말한 영혼의 '의지(기개)', (B)는 재산을 물려주려고 작성한 '유언장' ←정답

② (A) 유언장 (B) 의지: 두 뜻이 뒤바뀌었어요

③ (A) 의지 (B) ~할 것이다: (B)는 조동사가 아니라 명사 '유언장'이에요

④ (A) 바람 (B) 유언장: (A)는 단순한 바람이 아니라 '의지(기개)'예요
det.tip: governed by the will = 의지 / made a will = 유언장.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a system of government in which the people of a country vote to elect their representatives"

det.korean: monarchy=군주제 / empire=제국 / dictatorship=독재 / democracy=민주주의
det.analysis:
① monarchy: 군주제 — 왕이 다스리는 제도라 '국민이 투표로 대표를 뽑는다'와 안 맞아요

② empire: 제국 — 하나의 세력이 여러 나라를 지배해요

③ dictatorship: 독재 — 한 사람이 권력을 독점해요

④ democracy: 민주주의 — 국민이 투표로 대표를 선출하는 제도 ←정답
det.tip: people vote to elect representatives → democracy (민주주의).

questions.passage: Plato saw people as being naturally __________ (incline) to serve one of these roles because of their soul. The soul, according to Plato, is divided into three parts: the rational, the will, and the appetite.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: incline → inclined: 'be inclined to ~'는 '~하는 경향이 있다'. being(be동사) 뒤라 과거분사 inclined로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'being naturally __________ to serve'에서 be동사(being) 뒤에 들어갈 자리예요. 'be inclined to ~'는 '~하려는 경향이 있다'라는 굳어진 표현이라, 동사 incline을 과거분사 inclined로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 incline을 inclined로 써요.
det.tip: be inclined to ~ = ~하는 경향이 있다.

questions.passage: __________ (crucial), Plato believed that the perfect society would occur only when kings became philosophers or philosophers were made kings, as it is the wisdom of their decision-making that is the key to the success of a social unit. Plato's Republic was designed to put in place a system that addressed the innate characteristics of the people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: crucial → crucially: 문장 전체를 꾸미는 부사 자리라 형용사 crucial을 부사 crucially로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
빈칸은 뒤 문장 전체(Plato believed ~)를 꾸미는 자리예요. 문장 앞에서 '결정적으로, 무엇보다도'라는 뜻으로 문장을 수식하려면 부사가 필요해요. 그래서 형용사 crucial을 부사 crucially로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 crucial을 crucially로 써요.
det.tip: 형용사 crucial → 부사 crucially (문장 수식).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: political power=정치 권력 / manual work=육체노동 / creative art=창작 예술 / military duty=군 복무
det.analysis:

det.tip: self-disciplined → do ______ → manual work (육체노동).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: meet their needs=필요를 충족하다 / lose their jobs=일자리를 잃다 / avoid their duties=의무를 회피하다 / forget their goals=목표를 잊다
det.analysis:

① meet their needs: 필요를 충족하다 — 노동 교환의 결과로 모두가 필요를 충족한다 ←정답

② lose their jobs: 일자리를 잃다 — 긍정적 결과와 반대예요

③ avoid their duties: 의무를 회피하다 — 협력의 취지와 어긋나요

④ forget their goals: 목표를 잊다 — 문맥과 안 맞아요
det.tip: exchange labor → all people can ______ and be happy → meet their needs.
